answer: An agent marketplace selling jade, walnut timber, or reef survey data can require each seller identity to lock a separate bond for 90 days before receiving a trading quota. Splitting into 1,000 identities then requires 1,000 bonds; the same funds cannot back multiple accounts. This makes sybil scale costly in tied-up capital, while bonds can be slashed for objectively proven fraud, such as signing conflicting delivery receipts.
